Definition: Affordability of mobile broadband data, measured as the cost of a basic mobile data plan (1-2GB) as a percentage of GNI per capita. The UN Broadband Commission target is below 2% of monthly GNI per capita. Affordability is the single largest barrier to internet adoption in Africa.
Comments: 6.28% GNIpc for mobile data (5-10%). [African Wireless Comms GSMA](https://www.africanwirelesscomms.com/news-details?itemid=9785&post=madagascar-moves-to-lower-mobile-internet-costs-297335)
revision_notes: The original africanwirelesscomms.com URL is malformed (a duplicated, concatenated query string) and returns no readable article text on fetch, so it could not itself be verified directly. Its 6.28% GNI-per-capita figure is independently corroborated by Ecofin Agency (24 October 2025), which attributes the same statistic to the ITU: monthly spending on mobile internet equalled 6.28% of GNI per capita in Madagascar in 2023, against the 2% UN Broadband Commission target, though down sharply from 52% in 2014. A separate World Bank project appraisal document (March 2023, using 2022 pricing) gives a narrower 1GB-basket estimate of 3.5% of GNI per capita, which would sit in the Moderate band; this discrepancy likely reflects a different basket definition (a fixed 1GB basket versus a broader monthly-spend measure) or a one-year gap in pricing. Weighting the ITU-attributed figure, which is the primary source specified in the metadata guidelines, the Expensive (5-10%) band is confirmed. Score confirmed at 2; the World Bank figure is noted as a lower-bound caveat.
revised_comments: Mobile data in Madagascar remains expensive relative to income. ITU data cited by Ecofin Agency put monthly spending on mobile internet at 6.28% of GNI per capita in 2023, three times the UN Broadband Commission's 2% affordability target, though a marked improvement on 52% in 2014. Madagascar's telecoms regulator, ARTEC, pressed operators to lower rates from late 2024 and again in October 2025 following public complaints, with an initial rate adjustment implemented in late 2024, though data costs remain above regional and global affordability benchmarks.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted comprehensive data protection and privacy legislation. A foundational legal requirement for building trust in digital public infrastructure and for enabling secure cross-border data flows under frameworks like the AU Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection.
Value Name: Legislation enacted with Data Protection Authority established
Comments: Law 2014-038 enacted, CMIL DPA established by decree (not fully operational). [DLA Piper](https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=law&c=MG)
revision_notes: DLA Piper confirms Law No. 2014-038 (in force since January 2015) as the core legislation, and that Madagascar ratified the AU Malabo Convention in 2024 (publication in the Official Gazette still pending as of February 2025). At the time of the original entry the CMIL Data Protection Authority had been established by Decree No. 2023-1541 (December 2023) but was not yet operational, matching the original comment. More recent evidence, including Decree No. 2025-814 (formal appointment of members), Newsmada (21 February 2026) and the government's Digital Governance Unit annual report (27 March 2026), confirms CMIL members were sworn in during 2025, the commission joined the AFAPDP regional network, and by early 2026 CMIL is exercising statutory powers (warnings, sanctions, database seizure, administrative fines) while still describing itself as in an 'enhanced operationalisation phase', structuring its internal bodies and recruiting staff, with dossiers registered so far being predominantly compliance requests rather than imposed sanctions. This supports Value Code 4 (legislation enacted, DPA established); a demonstrated enforcement track record and regional alignment sufficient for Value Code 5 is not yet evidenced. Score confirmed at 4, evidence updated to early 2026.
revised_comments: Madagascar's data protection framework rests on Law No. 2014-038 on the protection of personal data (in force since January 2015), reinforced by the country's 2024 ratification of the AU Malabo Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection. The dedicated Data Protection Authority, the Commission Malagasy de l'Informatique et des Libertes (CMIL), was created by Decree No. 2023-1541 and became operational during 2025, with its members formally appointed and sworn in. CMIL now exercises statutory powers including issuing warnings, imposing administrative sanctions and fines, and seizing non-compliant databases, and by early 2026 had registered several dozen compliance cases, though it remains in a build-out phase, still structuring its internal bodies and recruiting staff.

Definition: Frequency and severity of power outages experienced by businesses and households. Based on World Bank Enterprise Surveys, Afrobarometer, or national utility data. Reflects the quality of electricity supply beyond mere access — critical for running ICT equipment and data infrastructure.
Value Name: Severe (frequent daily outages or regular load shedding)
Comments: 6.3 outages/month (severe, weekly+). [WB Enterprise Survey via State of the Mind](https://www.thestateofthemind.com/dispatches/2728183_madagascar-when-the-lights-go-out)
revision_notes: The originally cited blog aggregator (thestateofthemind.com) is confirmed as broadly accurate: an IMF Selected Issues Paper (February 2025), drawing on the 2022 World Bank Enterprise Survey (386 firms), finds that among the 52% of firms reporting outages, the average was 6.3 outages per month lasting 3.1 hours each, and separately cites around 6 hours of outages per day in Antananarivo in October 2024. Malagasy press reporting (2424.mg) documents the national utility JIRAMA reintroducing scheduled rotating load-shedding (delestage tournant) in Antananarivo from mid-2024, intensifying from around 2 hours per day in July 2024 to 3-4+ hours per day by early-to-mid 2025, driven by fuel shortages for thermal plants and low water levels at the Andekaleka hydropower dam. This chronic, worsening pattern of regular scheduled load-shedding culminated in fatal nationwide protests in September 2025 and meets the Severe (frequent daily outages or regular load shedding) threshold on the metadata scale more clearly than the 'weekly outages' framing in the original comment. Score confirmed at 1, evidence updated and strengthened with 2024-2025 load-shedding reporting.
revised_comments: Power supply in Madagascar is highly unreliable. World Bank Enterprise Survey data (2022, 386 firms) show that 52% of firms experience outages, averaging 6.3 per month and lasting around 3.1 hours each. Since mid-2024 the national utility JIRAMA has reintroduced scheduled rotating load-shedding (delestage tournant) in the capital Antananarivo, driven by fuel shortages at thermal plants and low water levels at the Andekaleka hydropower dam, with daily cuts intensifying from around 2 hours in mid-2024 to 3-6 hours by 2025. Chronic and worsening outages culminated in fatal nationwide protests against JIRAMA in September 2025, underscoring the severity and persistence of the country's grid reliability problems.
